chunk_findings.detail: `_signals` treats a later normal `lease.released` (`completed`, `done`, `merged`) as “no stop reason” by setting `text = ""`, but then the `if who and text.strip() and ...` guard prevents that event from updating the agent’s record at all. A previous stop reason therefore survives the newer normal release and can still classify the lane. For example, with `cfg.lanes.fleet_failed_patterns = ["429"]`, a lane `a` whose ledger state is `S.UNFINISHED` (item unfinished, lease released, item not terminal), and events `lease.expired holder=a reason="HTTP 429" ts=...:10Z` followed by `lease.released holder=a note="completed" ts=...:20Z`, `_signals` still returns the `...:10Z` reason `"HTTP 429"`. `registry` then lists the lane as `failed` with stop reason `"HTTP 429"`, even though the newest stop event was a completed release.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/fleet.py:_signals

chunk_findings.detail: The target-contract contradiction from previous finding 2 is still present. The new docs still tell the user to run `ddflow lanes brief <agent>`, while the declared second positional in `ddflow/surfaces/declared/lanes.py` says `with brief or resume: the lane name, or a unique part of it`, and the call only forwards that positional as `lane=a.get("lane")`. If agent names and lane names are not identical, a user following the docs runs `ddflow lanes brief worker-1` with an agent identity, but the surface/API treats `worker-1` as a lane name; a user following the parameter help runs `ddflow lanes brief feature-x` with a lane name, but the docs describe the brief target as an agent. The added parenthetical “a lane is an agent identity” does not remove the contradiction because the same doc line mixes `<lane>` for `resume` with `<agent>` for `brief`, and the CLI `view` help still says `resume <agent>` while the `lane` help says lane name.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/drivers/deltas/fleet-registry.md:10

chunk_findings.detail: Adding `""` to `_RELEASE_OK` treats an empty `lease.released` note as a normal completion, so it erases an earlier actionable stop reason even when the release is only a cleanup after an abnormal stop. Concrete input: agent `a` gets `lease.expired` with reason `"HTTP 429"` while its lane state is `S.UNFINISHED`; the ledger then emits `lease.released` with note `""` for the forced/cleanup release. `_signals` sees the empty note as `_RELEASE_OK`, clears the `"HTTP 429"` reason, and `a` no longer matches `cfg.lanes.fleet_failed_patterns = ["429"]`; it is not classified `failed`, so the orphaned unfinished item is not listed or resumed. An empty note means the release supplied no note, not that the earlier stop was cured.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/fleet.py:_RELEASE_OK

chunk_findings.detail: `_lease_left` treats a lease as held only by calling `ls.live(now, grace_s)`, then reports seconds left from `renewed_at + ttl_s - now` with grace omitted. Given `renewed_at=100`, `ttl_s=10`, `grace_s=30`, `now=115`, and `ls.holder == ln.name`, `live` is true (still inside grace) but the function returns `max(0, int(100+10-115)) == 0`. The field contract says `0` means the lane holds no live lease, so a listing or resume check that uses `lease_s == 0` treats this holder as idle and can offer a second restart while the lease is still live.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/fleet.py:_lease_left

chunk_findings.detail: `_signals` still cannot clear an older stop reason when the lane ledger still classifies the lane as stopped-unfinished. The new `registry` clearing only applies when `ln.state not in _STOPPED`, so if `LN.build` returns a lane in `S.UNFINISHED` after a later successful `lease.released`, the old reason remains. For example, with lane `alice` in a stopped-unfinished state for item `i`, events `lease.expired` at `ts="1"` with `holder=alice`, `reason="HTTP 429"`, then `lease.released` at `ts="2"` with `holder=alice`, `note="completed"`, and a failure pattern matching `HTTP 429`, `_signals` returns `("1", "HTTP 429")` because the successful release is converted to empty text and the guard skips updating `out`. `registry` keeps that reason and `_class` returns `FAILED`, even though the newest stop event in the log was a successful release.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/fleet.py:73

chunk_findings.detail: The new text says `ddflow lanes resume <lane>` is "eligible only while its item is unfinished and not held by someone else; otherwise it names the new holder." The "otherwise" case includes a lane whose item is finished (`done` is listed as a fleet class in the same paragraph), and for that case there is no new holder to name. A user following this doc for a done lane would expect the command to name a holder when it actually cannot; the doc should say finished items are simply not resumable.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/drivers/deltas/fleet-registry.md:14

chunk_findings.detail: `strip` filters with `if k != ticking`, where `ticking` is a tuple and `k` is a string key. A string is never equal to that tuple, so the condition is always true and it strips nothing. The comment says `heartbeat_age_s` and `lease_s` both count from the moment of the call, so the test intentionally needs to exclude them when comparing CLI and MCP outputs. Because this condition is boolean always-true, e.g. `run_cli` at t=0 returns `lease_s=0` while the later `rpc_call` at t=1 returns `lease_s=1`; the comparison `strip(cli["fleet"]) == strip(mcp["fleet"])` then fails even if the business fields match. It should be `if k not in ticking`.

chunk_findings.detail: `_signals` treats a later normal `lease.released` (`completed`, `done`, `merged`) as “no stop reason” by setting `text = ""`, but then the `if who and text.strip() and ...` guard prevents that event from updating the agent’s record at all. A previous stop reason therefore survives the newer normal release and can still classify the lane. For example, with `cfg.lanes.fleet_failed_patterns = ["429"]`, a lane `a` whose ledger state is `S.UNFINISHED` (item unfinished, lease released, item not terminal), and events `lease.expired holder=a reason="HTTP 429" ts=...:10Z` followed by `lease.released holder=a note="completed" ts=...:20Z`, `_signals` still returns the `...:10Z` reason `"HTTP 429"`. `registry` then lists the lane as `failed` with stop reason `"HTTP 429"`, even though the newest stop event was a completed release.

chunk_findings.detail: The target-contract contradiction from previous finding 2 is still present. The new docs still tell the user to run `ddflow lanes brief <agent>`, while the declared second positional in `ddflow/surfaces/declared/lanes.py` says `with brief or resume: the lane name, or a unique part of it`, and the call only forwards that positional as `lane=a.get("lane")`. If agent names and lane names are not identical, a user following the docs runs `ddflow lanes brief worker-1` with an agent identity, but the surface/API treats `worker-1` as a lane name; a user following the parameter help runs `ddflow lanes brief feature-x` with a lane name, but the docs describe the brief target as an agent. The added parenthetical “a lane is an agent identity” does not remove the contradiction because the same doc line mixes `<lane>` for `resume` with `<agent>` for `brief`, and the CLI `view` help still says `resume <agent>` while the `lane` help says lane name.

chunk_findings.detail: Adding `""` to `_RELEASE_OK` treats an empty `lease.released` note as a normal completion, so it erases an earlier actionable stop reason even when the release is only a cleanup after an abnormal stop. Concrete input: agent `a` gets `lease.expired` with reason `"HTTP 429"` while its lane state is `S.UNFINISHED`; the ledger then emits `lease.released` with note `""` for the forced/cleanup release. `_signals` sees the empty note as `_RELEASE_OK`, clears the `"HTTP 429"` reason, and `a` no longer matches `cfg.lanes.fleet_failed_patterns = ["429"]`; it is not classified `failed`, so the orphaned unfinished item is not listed or resumed. An empty note means the release supplied no note, not that the earlier stop was cured.

chunk_findings.detail: `_lease_left` treats a lease as held only by calling `ls.live(now, grace_s)`, then reports seconds left from `renewed_at + ttl_s - now` with grace omitted. Given `renewed_at=100`, `ttl_s=10`, `grace_s=30`, `now=115`, and `ls.holder == ln.name`, `live` is true (still inside grace) but the function returns `max(0, int(100+10-115)) == 0`. The field contract says `0` means the lane holds no live lease, so a listing or resume check that uses `lease_s == 0` treats this holder as idle and can offer a second restart while the lease is still live.

chunk_findings.detail: `_signals` still cannot clear an older stop reason when the lane ledger still classifies the lane as stopped-unfinished. The new `registry` clearing only applies when `ln.state not in _STOPPED`, so if `LN.build` returns a lane in `S.UNFINISHED` after a later successful `lease.released`, the old reason remains. For example, with lane `alice` in a stopped-unfinished state for item `i`, events `lease.expired` at `ts="1"` with `holder=alice`, `reason="HTTP 429"`, then `lease.released` at `ts="2"` with `holder=alice`, `note="completed"`, and a failure pattern matching `HTTP 429`, `_signals` returns `("1", "HTTP 429")` because the successful release is converted to empty text and the guard skips updating `out`. `registry` keeps that reason and `_class` returns `FAILED`, even though the newest stop event in the log was a successful release.

chunk_findings.detail: The new text says `ddflow lanes resume <lane>` is "eligible only while its item is unfinished and not held by someone else; otherwise it names the new holder." The "otherwise" case includes a lane whose item is finished (`done` is listed as a fleet class in the same paragraph), and for that case there is no new holder to name. A user following this doc for a done lane would expect the command to name a holder when it actually cannot; the doc should say finished items are simply not resumable.

chunk_findings.detail: `strip` filters with `if k != ticking`, where `ticking` is a tuple and `k` is a string key. A string is never equal to that tuple, so the condition is always true and it strips nothing. The comment says `heartbeat_age_s` and `lease_s` both count from the moment of the call, so the test intentionally needs to exclude them when comparing CLI and MCP outputs. Because this condition is boolean always-true, e.g. `run_cli` at t=0 returns `lease_s=0` while the later `rpc_call` at t=1 returns `lease_s=1`; the comparison `strip(cli["fleet"]) == strip(mcp["fleet"])` then fails even if the business fields match. It should be `if k not in ticking`.

chunk_findings.detail: `_lease_left` now adds `grace_s` to the remaining lease time even while the lease is still inside its TTL. For a live lease with `renewed_at == now`, `ttl_s=60`, `grace_s=30`, and `ls.live(now, 30)` true, the expression returns `max(1, int(0 + 60 + 30 - 0)) = 90`, so `ddflow lanes fleet` reports 90 seconds left on a 60-second lease. `grace_s` is only the post-expiry hold period, and the docs still describe this field as "seconds left on its lease"; the pre-change expression correctly returned 60.
